title: Test-user cleanup can delete unrelated real accounts
reasoning: The create command generates users with a specific prefix-shaped username, but the removal command selects any username containing the substring "testuser". With --all_test_users it deletes every matching account in the database, and in the fast-scoped path it deletes every matching account associated with the fast. A legitimate account such as "contestuser@example.com" or "mytestuser@example.com" would match and be deleted, even though it was not created by this command.
recommendation: Constrain deletion to the exact generated namespace, for example username starts with "testuser_" and ends with "@example.com", or better persist a dedicated marker/group/flag for generated accounts and only delete users carrying that marker. Keep dry-run behavior but make the destructive query use the stricter predicate.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for these management commands, and there is no evidence of a test that creates a non-generated user with "testuser" embedded in the username and verifies it survives cleanup.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create one generated-looking account and one normal account whose username merely contains "testuser", run the remove command with both fast-scoped and --all_test_users modes, and assert only the generated account is deleted.
minimumFixScope: Update remove_test_users_for_fast.py query predicates and add focused management-command tests for the deletion filters.

history.reasoning: The original evidence paths still exist, but the vulnerable substring predicates are no longer present. create_test_users_for_fast.py still creates usernames shaped like `testuser_{8-hex}_{fast_id}_{index}@example.com` at lines 79-88. remove_test_users_for_fast.py now defines `GENERATED_TEST_USER_USERNAME_REGEX = r"^testuser_[0-9a-f]{8}_[0-9]+_[0-9]+@example\.com$"` at line 9 and uses `username__regex=GENERATED_TEST_USER_USERNAME_REGEX` for both `--all_test_users` and fast-scoped deletion at lines 50-62, so accounts like `contestuser@example.com` or `mytestuser@example.com` no longer match. Focused regression tests now exist in tests/unit/hub/test_remove_test_users_command.py and cover both deletion modes preserving non-generated usernames. I attempted to run the test module through the documented Docker command, but Docker was unavailable in this environment (`docker.sock` missing), so the conclusion is based on current code plus the checked-in regression tests rather than a successful test run.
commands: docker exec bahk_devcontainer-app-1 python manage.py test tests.unit.hub.test_remove_test_users_command --settings=tests.test_settings
